function.arguments: {"observation": "The cross-tabulation of `channel` and `customer_segment` shows a severe imbalance: the email channel has 131 loyal customers and 131 returning customers, but only 64 new customers. In contrast, the paid_search channel has 304 new customers, 153 returning, and only 26 loyal customers. This imbalance means that the email channel was targeted at high-value customers, and the paid_search channel reached mostly new customers.", "implication": "The raw comparison of average revenue between channels is confounded by `customer_segment`. Since the email channel was deliberately targeted at loyal and returning customers (who are higher spenders), any observed difference in revenue is not necessarily due to the campaign itself, but due to the customer mix. Therefore, a simple comparison of average revenue is invalid. The analysis must either stratify by segment or adjust for segment using modeling (e.g., regression). Failure to do so would attribute the higher revenue to the campaign when it is actually due to targeting."}
